Chris Brown and Usher's feud history spans a 2023 Vegas confrontation, their 2025 reunion, and fresh backstage drama reported during their 2026 Atlanta tour.

Actual Article Body:
Usher and Chris Brown

Chris Brown and Usher have spent two decades moving between musical partnership, public praise and reported personal tension, making their rumored feud more complicated than a single backstage argument. The questions resurfaced after their November 5, 2026, concert in Atlanta, but the history begins long before The R&B Tour.

When Brown broke into music in 2005, Usher was already an established R&B star. Brown’s dancing and stage presence invited comparisons to the older performer, whose success provided an obvious reference point for a young singer building his career. Instead of becoming permanent public rivals, they developed a working relationship that produced records and shared performances.

In 2014, Chris Brown enlisted Usher and Rick Ross for “New Flame,” with all three appearing in the music video. Usher later joined Brown and Zayn Malik on the “Back to Sleep” remix, officially released on February 26, 2016. Brown, Usher and Gucci Mane followed with “Party” in December 2016. Those releases established a collaborative catalog that would eventually become central to their stadium shows.

Their connection was still strong publicly in April 2023. During an interview with Big Boy published on April 24, 2023, Usher discussed the possibility of facing Brown in a Verzuz-style event or sharing a bigger stage. “I love Chris,” he said, describing the younger star as his “little brother.” He presented a joint performance as a celebration of their mutual respect, not a battle over who belonged at the top.

Then came Chris Brown’s 34th birthday celebration in Las Vegas on the night of May 5, 2023, extending into May 6, 2023. At Skate Rock City, video showed the singers in a heated exchange. The confrontation began after Brown became upset with Teyana Taylor and Usher stepped in. The footage established an argument but did not show the alleged physical attack that later dominated headlines.

Witnesses claimed Usher followed Brown and his entourage outside and later emerged with what appeared to be a bloody nose.

On May 6, 2023, both artists performed as planned at the Lovers & Friends festival in Las Vegas. Photographs and videos from their appearances did not show obvious injuries. Chris Brown later addressed a separate backstage commotion at the festival, explaining that security was clearing an area where his child was present.
